title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a ring (later noetherian, then regular noetherian). The objects are '½-simplicial' k-modules L., which I read as semi-simplicial: face operators only, no degeneracies. L^! denotes the chain complex attached to L. 'by Dold–Puppe', a normalized complex. The neighbouring pages make clear the intended dictionary: rank L_n = Σ_i rk(L^!_i)·binom(n,i). This is the Dold–Kan count, since the number of surjections [n]→[i] is binom(n,i).

Def. 1. L. is called ∂-pseudo-coherent (resp. strictly ∂-pseudo-coherent, ∂-perfect, strictly ∂-perfect) when L^! is pseudo-coherent (resp. strictly pseudo-coherent, perfect, strictly perfect) in the sense of SGA 6.

Prop. 1.
(a) Strictly ∂-pseudo-coherent (resp. strictly ∂-perfect) holds iff the L^!_n are finitely generated projective (resp. and almost all zero). This is essentially the definition.
(b) Strictly ∂-pseudo-coherent holds iff the L_n themselves are finitely generated projective.
(c) Structure theorem: L. is strictly ∂-perfect iff it is a finite successive extension of the 'elementary' semi-simplicial modules Λ^iE ⊗ M_i, with M_i finitely generated projective. Here E is the basic semi-simplicial module of 'rank n' in degree n, a K(Z,1)-type object, so that Λ^iE has rank binom(n,i) and is the semi-simplicial avatar of K(Z,i), i.e. of Z[i] (décalage Λ^i(Z[1]) ≃ Z[i]). The filtration can be ordered by increasing i. A marginal addition gives an equivalent criterion, with Grothendieck's own '(?)': the L_n are finitely generated projective and n ↦ rk L_n is a polynomial function.
(d) For k noetherian: ∂-pseudo-coherence iff the L^!_n (equivalently the L_n) are of finite type.
(e) For k regular noetherian: ∂-perfect iff the L_n are of finite type and the fibrewise rank function is polynomial.

The next page completes (e). The rank n ↦ rk_{k(x)} L_n⊗k(x) is polynomial for large n. Its coefficients in the basis binom(n,i) are the fibre ranks of L^!_i and are constructible functions of x ∈ Spec k. Over non-regular rings one instead needs a strictly ∂-perfect L' → L inducing isomorphisms on the π_i.

The previous page asks a Macaulay-type question: which data (ν_j = rk π_j, polynomial f) are realized? Answer: write f − Σν_jP_j = Σμ_i binom(n+1,i); then need μ_0 = 0 and μ_i ≥ 0, with μ_0 = 0 ⇔ f(−1) = χ.

Purpose. Semi-simplicial, degreewise-finite models of perfect complexes have a polynomial 'rank function' playing the role of a Hilbert polynomial, with a numerical realizability criterion and constructibility over the base. The next page announces 'une théorie de la stabilité' for strictly ∂-perfect L. This looks like the beginning of a moduli/GIT-style programme for perfect complexes, using semi-simplicial models as the analogue of graded modules.
errors: The polynomiality criterion in (c) is marked '(?)' by Grothendieck himself. As stated (polynomial rank for all n), it needs care: one must specify 'for all n' versus 'for n large'. One must also exclude objects such as finite free semi-simplicial modules (e.g. Z[Δ^0]), whose rank is not polynomial and which are not filtered by Λ^iE⊗M.

There is an index inconsistency with the neighbouring pages. The previous page uses binom(n+1,i), and E there seems to have rank n+1; the next page uses binom(n,i). This depends on whether E is Z^{[n]} or its augmentation kernel; unresolved on the page.
(d) and (e) are fragmentary. Item (e) breaks off mid-sentence ('la fonction'), and the regularity hypothesis is needed, as the next page notes, so the non-regular case is open.

ideas.what: Notion of ∂-(pseudo-)coherent / ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules via the associated (Dold–Puppe) chain complex
ideas.modern_name: Perfect/pseudo-coherent objects transported along Dold–Kan to (semi-)simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA 6 (Illusie) for pseudo-coherent/perfect complexes; Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe for the correspondence
ideas.where_published: Perfect and pseudo-coherent complexes are defined in SGA 6 (Illusie, Exp. I); unsure whether the semi-simplicial variant appears anywhere

ideas.what: Structure theorem: strictly ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules are finite successive extensions of Λ^iE⊗M_i (exterior powers of a K(Z,1)-type object = models of M_i[i]), filtration ordered by i
ideas.modern_name: Dévissage of degreewise-finite simplicial models of perfect complexes; décalage Λ^i(M[1]) ≃ Γ^i(M)[i] / Dold–Puppe K(M,i)

ideas.what: Rank function n ↦ rk L_n as a 'Hilbert polynomial' of a semi-simplicial model; coefficients in basis binom(n,i) are ranks of the normalized complex; constructible in x ∈ Spec k; criterion for perfectness over regular rings via polynomiality
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial growth of OI^op-/Δ_inj-modules; Hilbert-type invariants for perfect complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Polynomiality for finitely generated FI/OI-modules: Church–Ellenberg–Farb (2015), Sam–Snowden (2017)

ideas.what: Over non-regular k: ∂-perfectness needs existence of a strictly ∂-perfect L' → L inducing isomorphisms on π_i (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Cofibrant/strict perfect replacement in the semi-simplicial model

missed.claim: Semi-simplicial modules are exactly contravariant functors on the category of finite ordered sets with injections (OI^op-modules). Grothendieck studies their rank growth n ↦ rk L_n, proves polynomiality, and gives a filtration by 'elementary' pieces Λ^iE⊗M_i. He then announces a 'théorie de la stabilité'. This prefigures the representation-stability / OI- and FI-module theory: Church–Ellenberg–Farb, Sam–Snowden, and Nagpal's filtrations by ♯-modules. That literature does not cite or connect to this Dold–Kan/perfect-complex viewpoint.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a homotopical interpretation (via Dold–Kan and décalage) of polynomiality and filtration results for OI^op-modules, and a dictionary between perfect complexes and finitely generated combinatorial-category representations.

missed.claim: There is a planned programme in which polynomial rank functions of semi-simplicial models of perfect complexes act as Hilbert polynomials. It includes a Macaulay-type realizability criterion (μ_0 = 0, μ_i ≥ 0; μ_0 = 0 ⇔ f(−1) = χ) and constructibility over Spec k. It aims at a 'stability theory', presumably towards moduli of perfect complexes à la GIT. The programme is not completed here.
missed.quote: les coefficients ... sont des fonctions constructibles en le point variable ∈ Spec k ... On veut une théorie de la stab. pour des L str. ∂-parfaits
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Moduli of perfect complexes were later built by Toën–Vaquié and Lieblich with stack methods. A Hilbert-scheme/GIT-style approach through degreewise-finite simplicial models with fixed rank polynomial seems unexplored and could give quasi-projective stratifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is mostly a careful dévissage of perfect complexes in semi-simplicial form, which is natural for Grothendieck. However, the polynomial rank function with constructible coefficients, the Macaulay-type realizability criterion, the filtration by Λ^iE⊗M_i, and the announced 'stability theory' anticipate both Hilbert-polynomial moduli of complexes and the OI-module/representation-stability circle of ideas. Neither link appears in the literature. Many details are hesitant ('?'), so this stays a moderate score.
transcription_corrections: In Prop 1 a) the condition is on the L^!_n (normalized complex), while b) is on the L_n themselves; the transcription has this right, but a) also includes '(resp. et nuls sauf un nb fini)'.
In c) the elementary pieces read 'Λ^i E ⊗ M_i (i ≥ 0)'; the ordering remark reads roughly '(l'ordre des facteurs dans une filtration croissante pouvant être choisi par ordre de i croissant)'.
The left marginal note inserted into c) reads approximately: 'ssi les L_n sont proj. de t.f. et f(n) = rg L_n fonction polynomiale (?) ... telles fonctions'.
'Donc th. = par déf. a) ci-dessous' is probably 'Donc ⇔ par déf. a) ci-dessous'.
e) begins 'Si k est noeth. régulier, L. est ∂-parfait ssi les L_n sont de t.f. et ... la fonction' and continues on the next page with n ↦ rg L_n ⊗ k(x).
